words.meaning: to spend a lot of money at once, usually on something enjoyable
words.example: After months of scrimping, she decided to splurge on a designer handbag.
words.persian: ریخت‌وپاش کردن، خرج زیاد و بی‌پروا کردن

words.meaning: to spend as little money as possible, saving by cutting costs tightly
words.example: They had to scrimp for a year to afford the down payment on the house.
words.persian: قناعت کردن، در خرج کردن خساست به خرج دادن

words.example: His profligate spending left the company insolvent within two years.
The parsimonious millionaire still darned his own socks.

words.meaning: displaying great wealth; luxurious and expensive-looking
words.example: The opulent hotel lobby was decorated with marble and gold.

words.meaning: to sell goods persistently, often going from place to place
words.example: He used to peddle cheap watches on the street before opening his own shop.

words.meaning: to turn something into a source of income
words.example: She monetized her cooking blog through ads and sponsorships.
words.persian: درآمدزایی کردن، پول‌سازی کردن از چیزی

words.meaning: to persuade a customer to buy something more expensive or additional
words.example: The salesman tried to upsell us to the premium package.
words.persian: تشویق مشتری به خرید گران‌تر یا بیشتر

words.example: The scandal had serious pecuniary consequences for the bank.
After the lawsuit, the once-thriving retailer became insolvent.

grammar.title: 6A: The Passive (all tenses)
grammar.explanation:
We form the passive with **be + past participle**: *was closed*, *are counted*, *has been damaged*. The tense always lives in the verb **be**.

Use the passive when the doer is unknown, obvious, or simply unimportant. The object of the active verb becomes the new subject: *A fortune was splurged on the launch* (we don't care who spent it).

Add **by + agent** only when the doer is important or surprising: *The recipe was monetized by a clever baker.* Without **by**, the focus stays on the action itself.

Negatives and questions follow the normal rules for **be**: *The tickets haven't been collected.* *Has the film been released yet?*

The passive loves processes and formal language. News and academic writing use it constantly: *The insolvent company will be sold.* *Goods are peddled on every corner.*
examples: *The boutique was closed* after two years of profligate spending. (past simple passive)
*Customers are upsold* at every counter in the store. (present simple passive, general truth)
*The recipe has been monetized* through a small online shop. (present perfect passive, recent result)
*The coins are counted* twice before the shop opens each morning. (passive for a process)
*The insolvent company will be sold* by the court next month. (future passive with by-agent)

practice.q: Your friend says: 'They stole my bike.' Rewrite the sentence in the passive.
When should you include 'by + agent' in a passive sentence?
practice.a: Only when the doer is important or surprising — for example, 'The cake was monetized by a clever baker.'
